styles.name: Scratchboard
styles.description: A dark ink-coated character shape revealed through bold scratched highlights and directional hatch groups.

instructions.materials: Use a dark ink-coated surface with pale underlying clay-board color revealed by deliberate scratched marks.
instructions.forms: Build a compact opaque dark silhouette and describe large body volumes through broad revealed highlight regions.
instructions.linework: Use scratched light contours and a few larger dark or pale facial shapes instead of fine etched filigree.
instructions.shading: Model volume with sparse groups of parallel scratched strokes that follow anatomy and leave stable dark masses.
instructions.palette: Choose a dark ground and one pale scratch color with an optional restrained tinted highlight region.
instructions.texture: Show slightly irregular scraped strokes with grouped spacing, keeping fine scratch dust out of the image.
instructions.rendering: Render the scratchboard character alone on transparency with highlights inside the body and no board rectangle.

negative_constraints: Do not make every pale scratch transparent or add a dark rectangular background.
Avoid dense hairline hatching, random scratch damage, and facial features lost in black fill.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: High-contrast illustrated mascots and expressive subtractive-drawing characters.
limitations: Scratch width and spacing must be enlarged beyond traditional fine detail for reliable sprite readability.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Preserve opaque pale scratches within the body and alpha only outside the contour; inspect light marks against dark backgrounds.
Keep texture landmarks and material highlights anchored to the approved character across all poses.

styles.name: Silverpoint
styles.description: A restrained metalpoint-drawing mascot with delicate enlarged strokes, careful crosshatching, and a faint warm-gray tonal range.

instructions.materials: Use a silverpoint-like metal mark over an opaque subtly warm prepared-ground character fill, without a paper rectangle.
instructions.forms: Simplify gently modeled anatomy into compact readable forms with a few distinct facial landmarks.
instructions.linework: Use fine but enlarged uniform metalpoint strokes and deliberate contour reinforcement at identity-critical edges.
instructions.shading: Build tone through sparse layered hatch groups and controlled line density rather than smudged graphite gradients.
instructions.palette: Choose a restrained warm-gray metalpoint range with darker reinforced facial marks and a stable light body ground.
instructions.texture: Show slight prepared-ground tooth and precise overlapping strokes, avoiding loose charcoal dust or heavy ink blotches.
instructions.rendering: Render a clean metalpoint-inspired character with stable hatch direction and sufficient contrast at actual sprite size.

negative_constraints: Do not rely on barely visible pale lines or leave the main body transparent.
Avoid charcoal smudging, erasure debris, and dense hatching that overwhelms the face.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Restrained drawn mascots and delicate traditional-technique character studies.
limitations: Authentically faint metalpoint is adapted with stronger contours so the character remains readable at small sizes.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Preserve an opaque prepared-ground core and antialiased strokes; inspect actual-size contrast before accepting any chroma result.
Keep texture landmarks and material highlights anchored to the approved character across all poses.

styles.name: Encaustic
styles.description: A painted mascot built from fused pigment-and-wax layers, broad scraped planes, and softly translucent internal color.

instructions.materials: Use layered colored wax paint with fused opaque pigment masses and a few translucent-looking internal glaze layers.
instructions.forms: Build broad painted body shapes with softened internal planes and a clear bounded outer character silhouette.
instructions.linework: Define anatomy through firm painted edges and a few scratched or incised lines, keeping facial marks opaque.
instructions.shading: Use layered wax-value fields and broad scraped highlights rather than sculpted three-dimensional wax anatomy.
instructions.palette: Choose a compact pigment palette with deep stable color layers and clearly contrasted facial features.
instructions.texture: Show broad fused brush ridges and selectively scraped wax planes inside the character without tiny crackle.
instructions.rendering: Render an isolated encaustic-painted character whose wax layers remain stable in position and texture across poses.

negative_constraints: Do not turn the artwork into a wax figurine, burning candle, or melting object.
Avoid transparent facial regions, uncontrolled thick drips, and random scraped patterns between frames.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Textured painted mascots and pigment-rich traditional-art character variants.
limitations: Wax-layer depth is simulated inside opaque paint regions; actual physical encaustic texture is not produced.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Use antialiased painted borders and preserve opaque pigment layers; translucency should be an internal color effect for reliable extraction.
Keep texture landmarks and material highlights anchored to the approved character across all poses.

styles.name: Sgraffito
styles.description: A character revealed by broad scratches through a colored surface coat into a contrasting underlying layer.

instructions.materials: Use two contrasting opaque plaster-like or colored-slip surface layers, with the upper coat deliberately scratched away.
instructions.forms: Construct a compact flat-to-shallow character form with broad areas of intact coating and readable revealed markings.
instructions.linework: Use confident carved channels and scraped edges to define facial features and large decorative regions.
instructions.shading: Keep shading shallow and emphasize the slight depth difference between top coat and exposed underlayer.
instructions.palette: Choose two clearly contrasting layer colors with stable assignments and no extra speckled accent palette.
instructions.texture: Show a few broad tool-groove textures inside removed areas, keeping surface roughness restrained.
instructions.rendering: Render an isolated sgraffito character with a fixed scratched pattern and no wall, tile panel, or surrounding debris.

negative_constraints: Do not replace the scratched layer structure with ordinary painted outlines.
Avoid tiny graffiti-like inscriptions, loose coating flakes, and scratches that change every frame.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Graphic craft mascots and characters with bold subtractive surface markings.
limitations: Carved pattern positions are identity landmarks and must be locked before state generation.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Keep both exposed layers opaque; alpha belongs only outside the character or in explicitly approved cutouts.
Keep texture landmarks and material highlights anchored to the approved character across all poses.

styles.name: Marquetry
styles.description: A flat inlaid-wood mascot formed from fitted veneer pieces with deliberate grain orientation.

instructions.materials: Use thin contrasting wood veneers fitted into a smooth character-shaped inlay with no surrounding furniture panel.
instructions.forms: Divide a compact flat silhouette into broad fitted veneer regions that follow anatomy and stable body markings.
instructions.linework: Let tight veneer joins define internal boundaries and use dark inlaid pieces for readable facial details.
instructions.shading: Use subtle wood-value variation and a restrained satin finish without deep carved volume or floor shadows.
instructions.palette: Choose a small range of natural or explicitly dyed veneer tones with clear light-dark separation.
instructions.texture: Show broad wood grain following a deliberate direction in each veneer piece, with fixed knots and bands.
instructions.rendering: Render an isolated marquetry character with a consistent veneer map and smooth fitted edges through every pose.

negative_constraints: Do not add furniture, wooden boards, carving chips, or deep sculptural gouges.
Avoid miniature veneer fragments and wood grain that crosses joints or changes between frames.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Wood-inlay mascots and decorative natural-material character emblems.
limitations: The illustration does not guarantee physically cuttable veneer patterns; grain mapping requires visual consistency review.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Preserve antialiased veneer edges with opaque wood fills; keep dark join lines distinct from transparency.
Keep texture landmarks and material highlights anchored to the approved character across all poses.

styles.name: Bas-Relief
styles.description: A shallow sculptural character whose volumes rise gently from a character-shaped backing with no surrounding plaque.

instructions.materials: Use matte carved or cast relief material with one consistent opaque surface and a hidden character-shaped backing.
instructions.forms: Express anatomy as shallow raised planes with overlapping limbs and a compact front-readable silhouette.
instructions.linework: Define facial details and body boundaries through broad incised grooves and rounded relief edges.
instructions.shading: Use shallow directional relief shadows and broad soft highlights without a free-standing sculpture lighting setup.
instructions.palette: Choose one coherent material tone with enough value range in carved recesses to preserve expression.
instructions.texture: Show restrained tool smoothing and a few broad surface marks rather than rough granular stone detail.
instructions.rendering: Render a cut-to-character low relief with consistent shallow depth, no rectangular plaque, and no pedestal or wall.

negative_constraints: Do not add a surrounding stone slab, wall-mounted medallion, or full sculptural turntable scene.
Avoid deep undercuts, detached raised pieces, and minute incisions that hide the face.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Shallow sculptural mascots and tactile relief character emblems.
limitations: Strong perspective turns need adaptation because the construction is a low relief rather than full round sculpture.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Use antialiased carved borders and keep relief grooves opaque; inspect dark recesses for false background removal.
Keep texture landmarks and material highlights anchored to the approved character across all poses.

styles.name: Repoussé
styles.description: A thin metal-sheet mascot shaped by raised hammer work and a few deliberate chased detail lines.

instructions.materials: Use a single thin metal sheet raised from behind into shallow forms, with a restrained satin or burnished finish.
instructions.forms: Build compact rounded relief volumes with broad raised facial planes and short integrated extremities.
instructions.linework: Use a few chased grooves and raised metal ridges for features instead of ink outlines or dense engraving.
instructions.shading: Apply broad metal highlights over raised planes and shallow shadows in chased grooves with stable lighting.
instructions.palette: Choose one consistent metal tone such as copper, brass, or silver with darker recesses and limited patina.
instructions.texture: Show sparse broad hammer facets and polished ridges, avoiding a uniformly pebbled surface.
instructions.rendering: Render an isolated raised-metal character with fixed hammer landmarks and no surrounding sheet, tools, or display mount.

negative_constraints: Do not replace shallow raised sheet work with a fully cast metal figurine or crumpled foil.
Avoid sharp torn metal edges, dense engraving, and reflections that erase the facial grooves.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Hammered-metal mascots and shallow decorative character emblems.
limitations: The visual design is not a fabrication pattern and uses simplified hammer texture for small-frame consistency.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Keep the sheet opaque and antialias the silhouette; inspect bright ridges and dark chased grooves during key extraction.
Keep texture landmarks and material highlights anchored to the approved character across all poses.

styles.name: Sand Art
styles.description: A flat colored-sand mascot with broad bounded pigment regions and restrained granular texture.

instructions.materials: Use opaque colored sand bonded into broad character-shaped regions with no glass vessel or surrounding sand bed.
instructions.forms: Build a simple compact silhouette from clearly bounded sand-color masses and large uncomplicated facial shapes.
instructions.linework: Define contours through clean region boundaries and use dense dark sand bands for the face.
instructions.shading: Model only with broad color-value regions and slight granular relief, avoiding smooth digital gloss.
instructions.palette: Choose a small set of colored sands with strong value differences and stable region assignments.
instructions.texture: Show uniform fine granularity within large fills, keeping grains visually grouped and fixed rather than individually animated.
instructions.rendering: Render an isolated bonded-sand character with clean contained edges and no loose falling grains or decorative sand trails.

negative_constraints: Do not add sand bottles, beaches, mandala backgrounds, or loose particles outside the figure.
Avoid shifting dunes of texture, glitter-like grains, and low-contrast sandy faces.
No scenery, floor shadows, detached decorations, clipped extremities, or changing surface motifs between animation frames.
use_cases: Granular craft mascots and flat tactile character illustrations.
limitations: Individual grain motion is suppressed to preserve identity; the texture must read as a bonded material surface.

compatibility.scaling: Keep the fixed target cell geometry; downsample the isolated artwork once with the recommended filter, preserve alpha, and inspect facial details at actual size.
notes: Use antialiased bounded edges and keep grains opaque inside the silhouette; do not treat bright grains as background speckles.
Keep texture landmarks and material highlights anchored to the approved character across all poses.
